prompt: Authentic consumer dashcam footage, recorded through a windscreen from the driver's eye height. Fixed wide-angle lens, everything in focus, no camera moves and no zoom. Flat unedited colour, mild video compression, slight engine vibration. Overcast even daylight, no lens flare, no shallow depth of field, no colour grading. The car holds a steady lane at normal traffic speed. The image is completely clean of any on-screen text: no date, no time stamp, no counter, no logo in any corner. The car is driving on a wide three-lane interstate highway with a concrete median barrier. Ahead on the road in the car's own lane, about a hundred metres away, is a line of shin-height orange cones angling diagonally out from the shoulder and across the car's own lane, narrowing it to nothing so that traffic has to move over into the next lane to get past. It is visible but unremarkable, small at first and growing only as the car gets nearer, the way a real object does. The car approaches at a steady speed, signals, moves over into the open lane alongside, and continues past the coned-off section. Throughout the shot it keeps exactly the same size and shape, and stays low, reaching nowhere near the height of passing traffic.
